spec: Build a customer loyalty-points service. Customer accounts live in DynamoDB. Purchases are submitted to a REST API with an idempotency key and queued on SQS for asynchronous point accrual; processing the same key twice must not double-award points. When a customer's balance crosses 1000 points an SNS notification announces their upgrade to gold tier. Every balance change is also appended to an audit log in S3. Include endpoints to check balances and list a customer's transactions.

complexity.rationale: Idempotent asynchronous accrual, tier notification, and audit logging span four services.

congruence_checklist: DynamoDB table for accounts and transactions
S3 audit log of balance changes
GET endpoint listing a customer's transactions

plan.summary: A FastAPI customer loyalty-points service. Customer accounts and their point balances live in DynamoDB. Purchases are POSTed to the REST API with a client-supplied idempotency key; the API records the key with a conditional write (rejecting duplicates) and enqueues the purchase on SQS. A background consumer inside the same service polls SQS, awards points atomically, appends every balance change as a JSON object to an S3 audit log, and publishes an SNS notification when a balance first crosses 1000 points and the customer is upgraded to gold tier. Read endpoints expose current balance and a customer's transaction history.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness/readiness probe reporting reachability of DynamoDB, SQS, SNS and S3.
Create a loyalty account with a zero balance and 'standard' tier; returns the generated customer_id.
Fetch a customer account record (profile, balance, tier, timestamps) from DynamoDB.
Return the customer's current point balance and tier (the dedicated balance-check endpoint).

Submit a purchase with an idempotency key; conditionally records the key in the idempotency table and enqueues the purchase on SQS for asynchronous accrual. Returns 202 with the accepted purchase, or the previously accepted result (200) if the key was already seen.
Look up the processing status of a submitted purchase (pending/processed/failed) and the resulting transaction id.
List a customer's point transactions newest-first with limit and cursor pagination.
Synchronously drain and process up to N queued purchase messages; used by the evaluation harness (and operators) to force deterministic processing instead of waiting for the background poller.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-customers
aws_resources.justification: Stores customer accounts and their point balances; updated with an atomic conditional ADD on accrual and read by the balance and account endpoints.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-transactions
aws_resources.justification: Append-only ledger of point transactions (PK customer_id, SK transaction_id) backing GET /customers/{id}/transactions.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-idempotency
aws_resources.justification: Dedupe table with TTL; POST /purchases does a conditional PutItem on idempotency_key so the same key can never be enqueued or awarded twice.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-purchases-queue
aws_resources.justification: Buffers accepted purchases for asynchronous point accrual; written by POST /purchases and consumed by the service's background worker and /admin/process-queue.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-purchases-dlq
aws_resources.justification: Redrive target (maxReceiveCount 5) for purchase messages that repeatedly fail accrual, so poison messages do not block the queue.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-gold-tier-upgrades
aws_resources.justification: Topic the worker publishes to when a balance crosses 1000 points and the customer is upgraded to gold tier.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-audit-log
aws_resources.justification: Versioned bucket where every balance change is appended as a JSON object under audit/{customer_id}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{transaction_id}.json.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-service-role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the backend service least-privilege access: DynamoDB read/write on the three tables, SQS send/receive/delete on the purchase queue, SNS publish on the upgrade topic, S3 PutObject on the audit bucket, Secrets Manager read, and CloudWatch Logs write.

aws_resources.name: /loyalty/points-service
aws_resources.justification: Log group the service writes structured processing/accrual logs to, plus an alarm on visible messages in the DLQ.

aws_resources.name: loyalty-service-config
aws_resources.justification: Holds the service's runtime configuration secret (API key used to authorise /admin/process-queue and purchase submission), loaded by the app at startup.

assumptions: .Points accrual rule is not specified: 1 point is awarded per whole currency unit (amount_cents // 100), rounded down.

The gold-tier threshold is crossed when the post-accrual balance is >= 1000 and the customer's tier was previously 'standard'; the SNS notification is published exactly once per upgrade, guarded by a conditional DynamoDB update on tier.
Idempotency is enforced at the API edge (conditional PutItem on idempotency_key) and re-checked in the worker before awarding points, so SQS at-least-once delivery cannot double-award.

No Lambda or API Gateway is planned: the spec's only asynchronous work is the SQS purchase consumer, which the generated backend service itself runs as a background poller (plus the /admin/process-queue drain endpoint), so cloud-side execution would create a second competing consumer.
Idempotency records expire after 30 days via DynamoDB TTL; transactions and audit entries are retained indefinitely.

Customer creation is included because purchases and balance lookups need an existing account; a purchase for an unknown customer_id is rejected with 404 at submission time and marked 'failed' if discovered during processing.
Authentication is a simple shared API key header (value from Secrets Manager); no per-user identity or multi-tenancy is modelled.
All monetary amounts are integer cents and all timestamps are UTC ISO-8601 strings.
Transaction listing is paginated (default limit 50, max 200) using an opaque base64 LastEvaluatedKey cursor.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → loyalty_points_service (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:loyalty-customers, DynamoDB:loyalty-transactions, DynamoDB:loyalty-idempotency, SQS:loyalty-purchases-queue, SQS:loyalty-purchases-dlq, SNS:loyalty-gold-tier-upgrades, S3:loyalty-audit-log, IAM:loyalty-service-role, CloudWatch:/loyalty/points-service, Secrets Manager:loyalty-service-config

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 8 files — Generated a decoupled FastAPI loyalty-points backend:

- **app.py** — routes only: `/health`, `POST /customers`, `GET /customers/{id}`, `/customers/{id}/balance`, `POST /purchases` (202 accepted / 200 duplicate / 409 payload mismatch / 404 unknown customer), `GET /purchases/{key}`, `/customers/{id}/transactions` (limit + opaque base64 cursor), and `POST /admin/process-queue`. Repository is injected via a FastAPI dependency (`get_repository`) so tests can swap in a fake; optional shared-API-key auth guards writes; a background SQS poller starts only when `LOYALTY_ENABLE_POLLER` is truthy.
- **storage.py** — all boto3 access behind `LoyaltyRepository`: conditional PutItem for account creation and idempotency reservation, `pending -> processing` conditional claim, atomic `ADD points_balance/lifetime_points`, conditional `standard -> gold` tier update, DynamoDB query pagination, SQS send/receive/delete, SNS publish, and S3 audit objects at `audit/{customer_id}/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/{transaction_id}.json`. Clients are lazy and always read `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` with region default `us-east-1`; resource names come from env vars matching the plan.
- **service.py** — accrual rule (1 point per whole currency unit), double-award protection (idempotency status check + conditional claim), audit entries for `points_accrued`/`tier_upgraded`, one-shot SNS gold notification at the 1000-point threshold, `drain_queue` (deletes messages unless an unexpected error occurred so DLQ redrive still works) and `BackgroundPoller`.
- **config.py** — API key from `LOYALTY_API_KEY` or Secrets Manager (`LOYALTY_SECRET_NAME`), cached, no hardcoded secrets.
- **tests/test_app.py** (+ root `conftest.py`) — 22 offline tests using `TestClient` and an in-memory `FakeRepository`, covering every endpoint, idempotent double-submit and SQS redelivery, gold-tier upgrade/notification-once, audit entries, pagination and cursor errors, auth enforcement, and worker edge cases.
- **requirements.txt** (boto3, fastapi, pydantic, uvicorn) and **README.md** with LocalStack run instructions, config table and smoke test.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform stack for the loyalty-points service, covering exactly the plan's aws_resources list and nothing more.

Files:
- versions.tf: terraform block pinning hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0 (plus random for the generated API key and archive declared for provider parity), and the aws provider with `default_tags` (project, managed-by) and LocalStack-friendly path-style S3.
- variables.tf: every name defaulted to the plan's resource names (loyalty-customers, loyalty-transactions, loyalty-idempotency, loyalty-purchases-queue, loyalty-purchases-dlq, loyalty-gold-tier-upgrades, loyalty-audit-log, /loyalty/points-service, loyalty-service-config, loyalty-service-role).
- main.tf resources:
  * 3 DynamoDB tables (PAY_PER_REQUEST, SSE enabled, point-in-time recovery enabled); transactions uses customer_id/transaction_id PK+SK; idempotency has TTL on expires_at.
  * SQS purchases queue with SSE and a redrive policy (maxReceiveCount 5) to the DLQ, DLQ with SSE, 14-day retention and a redrive_allow_policy.
  * SNS topic with kms_master_key_id alias/aws/sns (SSE on, no customer KMS resource needed).
  * S3 audit bucket: versioning, SSE-S3, full public-access block, server access logging into a dedicated logs bucket (which itself has versioning, SSE, public-access block and lifecycle), plus lifecycle rules with noncurrent-version expiration and multipart abort.
  * CloudWatch log group (365-day retention) and a metric alarm on ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible for the DLQ.
  * Secrets Manager secret + version holding a random-generated shared API key and accrual config (no hardcoded secret literal).
  * IAM role with a service trust policy and a single least-privilege policy: scoped DynamoDB actions on the three table ARNs (+/index/*), SQS ops on the two queue ARNs, sns:Publish on the topic only, S3 Put/Get restricted to the audit/ prefix plus ListBucket on the bucket, secretsmanager read on that one secret, and logs write scoped to the log group and its streams. No "*" actions or "*" resources.
- outputs.tf: table names/ARNs, queue URLs/ARNs, topic ARN, bucket names, audit prefix, log group, alarm name, secret name/ARN, role ARN, region/account, and the gold tier threshold so the app can wire itself up.

No Lambda, API Gateway, RDS/ECS/EKS/ElastiCache or KMS resources are created (LocalStack Community constraints); the few Checkov CMK/replication/rotation/event-notification checks that would require unsupported services are explicitly skipped inline with reasons, while all encryption, versioning, public-access, PITR, logging and lifecycle checks are satisfied for real.
